page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.12xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance designed for balanced compute, memory, and high-throughput local storage. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. The instance includes 192.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, and is without discrete graphics processing units.

A key component of the hardware configuration is the integration of 2850 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage. This local instance store provides low-latency, high-IOPS access suitable for scratch spaces, cache buffers, or transient operational data. Complementing the storage throughput is a dedicated network interface delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, enabling efficient data transfers for distributed processing.

From an infrastructure perspective, m8idb.12xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency by combining substantial core density, large memory capacity, and bundled local NVMe storage within a single general-purpose deployment. Workloads needing rapid disk operations do not require external block storage attachments for ephemeral datasets, though ephemeral data loss risks remain inherent to local instance stores upon termination. The instance is suited for relational and NoSQL databases requiring local caching, large-scale continuous integration and build pipelines, distributed analytical processing, and multi-tier enterprise web backends.
